title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit's pyproject.toml pins "websockets>=12.0.0". Version 16.1 of websockets (released July 9, 2026) introduced a change that blocks non-ASCII values in HTTP headers (see [changelog](https://websockets.readthedocs.io/en/stable/project/changelog.html#id2), "Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers").

This breaks the WebSocket handshake for setups where a reverse proxy / auth layer injects headers containing UTF-8 characters before the request reaches Streamlit — for example [Authelia](https://www.authelia.com/) forward-auth, which can inject a Remote-Name header containing the user's display name (e.g. accented characters, non-Latin scripts).

Since Streamlit's dependency constraint allows websockets to resolve to 16.1+, installing/upgrading Streamlit in a fresh environment can silently pull in a version that breaks WebSocket connections for any deployment relying on non-ASCII header values, with no warning at install time

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy Streamlit behind a reverse proxy (nginx/Traefik) with Authelia forward-auth, configured to forward Remote-Name, Remote-Email, etc. headers to the backend.
2. Ensure a user's Authelia display name contains a non-ASCII character (e.g. "François", "Müller", "田中").
3. Install/upgrade Streamlit in an environment where pip resolves websockets to >=16.1.
4. Log in as that user and attempt to load the app.

### Expected Behavior

The WebSocket connection (/_stcore/stream) should be established successfully, as it was with websockets<16.1.

### Current Behavior

The WebSocket handshake fails because websockets 16.1 rejects the non-ASCII header value. The app gets stuck on "Please wait..." / the frontend logs a WebSocket connection failure, similar in symptom to issues like #8799.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian
- Browser: Chrome / Mozilla


### Additional Information

Workaround: pinning websockets<16.1 restores normal behavior.

Possible fixes on Streamlit's side:

- Tighten the websockets dependency constraint (e.g. >=12.0.0,<16.1) until this is addressed, or

- Percent-encode / sanitize header values Streamlit forwards or reads internally before they reach the websockets layer.

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16030)

### Issue analysis

This is a **bug / upstream-dependency regression**. Streamlit's `lib/pyproject.toml` currently declares `websockets>=12.0.0,<17`, which still allows `websockets` to resolve to **16.1** (released 2026-07-09). That release "Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers", so any WebSocket handshake carrying a UTF-8 header value is now rejected.

Streamlit doesn't import `websockets` directly — it's used as **uvicorn's WebSocket protocol implementation** (`ws="websockets-sansio"` for uvicorn ≥ 0.44.0, else `"auto"`), configured in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_server.py` (`_get_websocket_protocol`). The handshake header parsing therefore happens inside the `websockets` layer. When a reverse proxy / forward-auth layer (e.g. Authelia injecting a `Remote-Name` with accented or non-Latin characters) forwards a non-ASCII header, `websockets` 16.1 rejects it and the `/_stcore/stream` handshake fails, leaving the app stuck on "Please wait...".

**Likely fixes** (as the reporter notes): tighten the constraint to exclude the broken range (e.g. `websockets>=12.0.0,<16.1` or skip 16.1) and/or sanitize/percent-encode forwarded header values before they reach the `websockets` layer. Note the concern is valid even with the existing `<17` cap, since 16.1 falls within it.

### Related Issues

- [#8799](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8799) — "WebSocket header HTTP_SEC_WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL value changed ... which gives connection error" (closed). Directly referenced by this issue; same failure class of a WebSocket handshake failing due to a header value.
- [#8188](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8188) — "Unnecessary failover on /_stcore/stream". Same symptom/deployment context: the `/_stcore/stream` WebSocket hangs/fails when running behind a reverse proxy.
- [#12108](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12108) — "Frequent websocket connection drops ...". Same pattern of an upstream WebSocket-layer dependency change (Tornado 6.5.1) breaking WebSocket connectivity for users behind proxies/Nginx.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `claude-opus-4-8-thinking-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. This looks like an intended change by `websockets` so there might be a valid reason to exclude non-ASCII header. It would be good if you report this to the https://github.com/python-websockets/websockets repo as well to get more clarity on why this was done.

We are seeing the same symptom, but the immediate exception is in **uvicorn**, not in websockets itself.

**Environment where we reproduced it:**
- Streamlit 1.58.0 / 1.59.2
- uvicorn 0.51.0
- websockets 16.1
- Python 3.10 / 3.14
- Reverse proxy: nginx + Authentik, forwarding user display-name headers (e.g. `X-authentik-name: Céline`)

**Traceback:**
```
  File ".../uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py", line 196, in <listcomp>
    (key.encode("ascii"), value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape"))
UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode characters in position 4-5: ordinal not in range(128)
```

**What's happening:**
- `websockets` 16.x decodes incoming HTTP header values as ISO-8859-1 (latin-1). A byte like `0xE9` therefore becomes the character `é` (U+00E9) by the time uvicorn sees it.
- `uvicorn 0.51.0` then tries to build the ASGI `headers` list with `value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")`.
- For a real non-ASCII character such as `é` (U+00E9) this is impossible, so the WebSocket handshake aborts.

**Note on the workaround `websockets<16.1`:** pinning websockets may avoid websockets-side validation, but it did **not** fix the above `UnicodeEncodeError` for us, because the crash is in uvicorn's re-encoding of the header value.

**Manual workaround:**
In `uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py`, in `handle_connect`, change the header listcomp so values are encoded back with `latin-1` (which preserves the original bytes, because websockets decoded them with latin-1):

```python
(key.encode("ascii"), value.encode("latin-1"))
```

**Suggested fix:**
Uvicorn should encode WebSocket header values with `latin-1` (or at least preserve the ISO-8859-1 decoded bytes) when building the ASGI `scope` in `websockets_sansio_impl.py`.
I think this issue can be closed in favor of https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/issues/3035, unless you want to keep it open until resolved in uvicorn.
Can you take care of filing the bug against Authelia? They should really not send non-ASCII headers.

### ✅ Confirmed — reproduced end-to-end

Reproduced on a clean environment. A fresh `pip install streamlit==1.58.0` silently resolves to the broken combination:

- `streamlit==1.58.0`, `uvicorn==0.51.0`, `websockets==16.1`

Streamlit 1.58 selects uvicorn's `websockets-sansio` protocol (uvicorn ≥ 0.44.0), so this is the affected path.

**Repro:** raw WebSocket handshake to `/_stcore/stream` simulating a forward-auth proxy injecting a display-name header:

| Header value | Result |
|---|---|
| `X-Authentik-Name: Celine` (ASCII) | `101 Switching Protocols` ✅ |
| `X-Authentik-Name: Céline` (raw byte `0xE9`) | connection dropped, **no response** ❌ |

Server traceback matches [USER]'s report exactly:

```
File ".../uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py", line 196, in handle_connect
    (key.encode("ascii"), value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape"))
UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character '\xe9' in position 1: ordinal not in range(128)
```

### Root cause (the precise regression)

The changelog phrase *"Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers"* is a little misleading for this case — websockets 16.1's header-value regex `[\x09\x20-\x7e\x80-\xff]*` still **allows** high bytes, so `0xE9` passes through. The actual break is a change in how the value is **decoded**:

- **websockets 16.0** — `http11.py`: `value = raw_value.decode("ascii", "surrogateescape")` → `é` becomes surrogate `U+DCE9`, which uvicorn's `value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")` round-trips cleanly back to `0xE9`. ✅
- **websockets 16.1** — `http11.py`: `value = raw_value.decode("iso-8859-1")` → `é` becomes the real char `U+00E9`, which uvicorn's surrogateescape re-encode **cannot** encode → `UnicodeEncodeError` → handshake aborts. ❌

(16.1's `parse_headers` docstring still claims *"Non-ASCII characters are represented with surrogate escapes,"* which no longer matches its own code — worth flagging upstream.)

### Two corrections/notes for triage

1. **Dependency constraint.** The current constraint (both `develop` and 1.58.0) is `websockets>=12.0.0` with **no upper bound** — not `<17`. So 16.1 (and anything newer) is fully permitted, and fresh installs pull it.
2. **Workaround discrepancy resolved.** The reporter says pinning `websockets<16.1` fixes it; [USER] says it didn't. In this exact stack (streamlit 1.58.0 / uvicorn 0.51.0), **`websockets==16.0` makes the non-ASCII handshake succeed** (101, no crash) — so the pin *does* work here. [USER]'s result was likely a different websockets/uvicorn combination (Authentik + Python 3.10/3.14).

### Possible Streamlit-side mitigations

- Add an upper bound / exclude the broken range in `lib/pyproject.toml` (e.g. `websockets>=12.0.0,!=16.1` or a tested cap), and/or
- Track the upstream fix — this is fundamentally a websockets 16.1 ↔ uvicorn incompatibility (uvicorn should re-encode with `latin-1` to preserve the ISO-8859-1 bytes websockets now produces).

> The changelog phrase "Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers" 

It referred to setting values in headers for outgoing HTTP messages, not parsing values in incoming messages. I plan to clarify the changelog.

As a stopgap measure, I just released websockets 16.1.1 which undoes the problematic change in 16.1.

The change will happen in websockets 17.0, where it's properly documented as a backwards incompatible change, and I'll work with the maintainer of uvicorn to fix the problem by then.

[USER], thanks for taking a look and doing a quick patch! With that patch, I'm going to close this issue here and will keep track of the [upstream uvicorn issue](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/issues/3035).
